First public release of **EatPoint**, a fork of [OpenNutriTracker](https://github.com/simonoppowa/OpenNutriTracker) that counts food in points: 1 point is 100 kcal of carbohydrate, protein or fat.

> **Preview build.** Installs as its own app (`io.github.grohle.eatpoint`), not on Google Play or the App Store yet. It updates earlier EatPoint test builds in place.

## What's new in 0.3

**Your diet**
- Diet (omnivore, pescatarian, vegetarian, vegan), religious diet (halal, kosher, Hindu), the 14 EU allergens, lactose and gluten intolerance, and foods you like or don't want. Asked during setup and editable any time in Settings.
- Intolerances keep the food in its free-from version (lactose-free milk, gluten-free bread); coeliac disease uses certified gluten-free versions; a milk allergy also rules out lactose-free milk and suggests plant-based instead.
- Logging a food, planning a dish, importing a menu and building a recipe warn you when something doesn't fit: what it contains, why, and what to choose instead.
- Scanning a nutrition label can also read the ingredients list ("Contains", "May contain traces of", "vegan", "gluten-free"…). Barcode products use Open Food Facts' allergens, traces and labels.

**Menu generator**
- Plans 1 to 14 days for your meals and points, on the phone (private, offline) or with your AI provider. It follows your diet, uses your own dishes first and suggests the foods you like. You review everything before it is saved.

**Weekly suggestions**
- The weekly menu points out fibre, oily fish (omega-3), vitamin B12 sources, pulses, fruit and vegetables, wholegrains, calcium and variety, as a guide.

**Fibre points**
- 1 fibre point = 5 g, with a daily minimum of 25 g split across your meals, shown on Home, when logging and in the menu.

**Household portions**
- Amounts also in pieces: "1½ chicken fillets", "½ avocado", "≈ 6 potatoes", when logging, in the menu and on the shopping list.

**Complete your meals**
- When logging, on Home ("What am I missing?") and in the recipe builder: what a meal still lacks and foods that would complete it, in household portions.

**Goals**
- New goals: build muscle, gain weight and muscle, and lose weight while building muscle, each with its own weekly pace and more protein. An (i) explains points, the lean-mass method and the calorie goal step by step.
- Choosing a goal now keeps the weekly pace in line with it.

**Menu dish picker**
- Search your dishes, the basic foods and the food databases at once; create a recipe from there when you have none.

**You tab**
- Settings have their own panel above your goal.

## Also in this release (from 0.2)
- **Your meals:** as many as you like, each with its own budget; overspending on one is taken off the meals still ahead.
- **Travel mode:** pause the menu, shopping list and reminders and just log what you eat.
- **Menu and recipe importer** from text, tables, files or photos.
- **Month calendar** of the weekly menu.
- **Points everywhere:** amount sheet with grams and points, nutrition label scanner, weekly menu with shopping list and reminders, household sync, an on-phone agent connector, and export of everything.

## Coming next
- A downloadable food database of basic foods and supermarket products, adapted to points, during setup or from Settings.
- More languages, with label and menu reading in each.

## Downloads
- `EatPoint-0.3.0-arm64-v8a.apk`: for almost every phone from the last few years.
- `EatPoint-0.3.0-universal.apk`: for any Android 8.0+ device.
